pr_title: net: sockets: Fix getsockname() fucntion and add tests to cover it
pr_body:
This PR relies on FIN handling being fixed in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/61353, as this interferes with the tests (the issue (context leak) was already present in the test suite, but it did not manifest itself until new tests involving TCP were added). So DNM for now.

This PR fixes `getsockname()` function operation, and adds tests to cover its functionality. 

Additionally, the PR fixes a corner case encountered in the TCP implementation which prevented the tests from running properly (i. e. tests were leaking net/TCP context, interfering with each other.

Fixes #61545
pr_comments: @ssharks Please specifically have a look at a fix in e2964b7986cd7533093af1377264d88daa03ad63. The issue was easily reproducible in those simple test cases, where both client and server ran from a single thread.

issue_context.title: net: getsockname: fails for bound socket
comments: The fix for me was removing the check, but I have not yet submitted a PR

That check indeed looks wrong as it covers only part of the cases, I think that `ctx->local` should be checked instead to verify whether the socket has been bound (either by explicit call to `bind()`, or as a result of `connect()` and others). In case `net_sin_ptr(&ctx->local)->sin_addr`/`net_sin6_ptr(&ctx->local)->sin6_addr` pointer is NULL, the function should report an error.
@rlubos - it also appears that `getsockname()` returns (at least) the port number in host byte order, but it should be returned in network byte order.

> @rlubos - it also appears that `getsockname()` returns (at least) the port number in host byte order, but it should be returned in network byte order.

I can't really reproduce what you say, I'm using your example code and can successfully connect with the port printed under `network byte order`. I can also see, that when I bind the socket to a specific port explicitly (`addr.sin_port = htons(10000);`), it is printed correctly after `ntohs()` conversion (so it was stored in the network byte order, as `struct sockaddr_in` requires).

> I can't really reproduce what you say, I'm using your example code and can successfully connect with the port printed under `network byte order`.

On Linux, that is what I expect, but I found it wasn't the case in Zephyr earlier today.

I'll give it a shot again.

review_comments: This break will skip any possible data received with the ACK. Are you deliberately ignoring this? This means that it might be retransmitted in FIN1 where it will receive a reset

In case there is no `accept_cb`, the data would not be processed anyway, as there would be no `recv_cb` registered, so yeah, `break` here was intentional. I think that a potential RST in FIN1 state in such case may actually be a reasonable choice, as this clearly indicates that the data was **not** delivered. WDYT?
Sounds like this ok, it would be code wist pretty nasty to send a RST from this point and go to TIME_WAIT.
